Class StraightIn

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.StraightIn
public final class StraightIn extends Object
With the opponent in view and out of reach, the strafe keys are let go of: it closes the distance running straight at the opponent. Going round someone is footwork for the range swords meet at, and there the strafe stays the network's.

Why it is a rule. The user, 18 October: it strafes while it moves in to get close; "just walk straight and only strafe when it is combo". An opponent that backed off in the middle of its combo was gone round in a circle to be got at, which is slower than running at it and looks wrong: the strafe plan (MixIdea) was handed out, and paid for, within five blocks.

Not in the ticks after a hit taken: a step to the side then is part of getting out of a combo. Nor with the opponent cut off by the edge of the screen, where its height on it says it is farther off than it is.
